title: Injected-thought reportability
takeaway: Adding a single J-lens vector to the residual stream at every token of the user turn makes the model report that concept when it is asked to introspect on its own state, in the majority of trials. The injected concept surfaces only at the moment the report is elicited, not elsewhere in the response, which is the paper's operational sense of a representation being verbalizable rather than an unconditional impulse to speak.
walkthrough:
This item is a live widget rather than a static image, paired with one summary plot. The widget replays an introspection conversation with [[jacobian-lens]] and next-token logit readouts attached to particular token positions; the plot summarizes the same intervention over many concepts. It is part of the paper's case for [[verbal-report]]: contents of the [[j-space]] are what the model can put into words on demand.

The protocol comes from prior introspection work ([[injected-thought-introspection]]). The model is told that a thought may have been implanted in its activations, and is asked to report what, if anything, it detects. When the response is prefilled ([[prefill]]) with a claim of having detected something, the most likely continuation is "elephant". The authors noticed that elephant also sits near the top of the J-lens readout on the user prompt itself, at the comma after "If so". That observation suggested the model answers the question partly by reading its own J-space at prompt positions.

The intervention tests this. A single [[j-lens-vector]] $v_t$, the direction that disposes the model to say token $t$, is added into the [[residual-stream]] at every token of the user turn, scaled by a steering strength ([[j-lens-steering]], $h \leftarrow h + \alpha v_t$). The response is then re-sampled. In the widget's example the injected vector is lightning, and readouts are taken at three kinds of position: the comma after "If so", the open quotation mark where the model names what it detected, and every other position of the assistant turn as a position control.

The model reports detecting lightning, and the injected concept dominates the readouts exactly at the quotation mark. At the control positions it does not surface in the next-token logits, so the injection is not a blanket push to say "lightning"; it becomes causally effective only when the introspective report is elicited. The adjacent plot tracks the [[median-reciprocal-rank]] of the injected concept in the model's output at the report position against steering strength, over $n = 100$ concepts, with an interquartile band. The paper states the result as the model reporting the injected concept in the majority of trials; the exact curve values live in the widget rather than in the text.

terms.definition: The lens's read operation at one position and layer: project the residual stream through the corpus-averaged Jacobian and the unembedding to score every vocabulary token. In the widget it shows which concepts occupy the workspace at each marked position.
The model's actual output scores over the vocabulary at a position, shown alongside the lens readout. Comparing the two separates what the model is about to say from what its workspace is carrying.
A prompt telling the model that a thought may have been implanted in its activations and asking it to report what, if anything, it detects. Adapted from prior work on model introspection.
The intervention $h \leftarrow h + \alpha v_t$: a scaled J-lens vector added to the residual stream, here at every token position of the user turn.
The scalar $\alpha$ multiplying the injected vector; the x-axis of the summary plot, swept over a range to show how report reliability grows with injection magnitude.

One vector per vocabulary token per layer: the direction in residual-stream space that, on average across contexts, disposes the model to say that token. One such vector per trial is what gets injected.

The y-axis of the summary plot: the reciprocal of the injected concept's rank in the model's output at the report position, with the median taken over the 100 concepts. A value of 1 means the injected concept is the top output.
The shaded region around the median curve spanning the 25th to 75th percentile of reciprocal ranks across the 100 concepts, showing spread across concepts at each strength.

The user-prompt position where the authors first noticed elephant at the top of the lens readout, and one of the marked readout sites. It is where the model appears to consult its J-space when deciding what it detected.
The assistant-turn position immediately before the model names the detected thought; the readout site where the injected concept's causal effect on the output appears.
Readouts taken at every other position of the assistant turn, to show that the injection does not push the concept into the output anywhere except the report moment.
The human side of the conversation. The injection is applied across all of its token positions, upstream of the model's response.
The model's response. Readouts here test where, if anywhere, the injected concept reaches the output.
Forcing the start of the model's response to be a chosen text and letting it continue. Prefilling a claim of detection is how the baseline "elephant" prediction was elicited.
The example concept injected in the widget's transcript; the model goes on to report detecting lightning.
The model's most likely answer when prefilled with a detection claim and nothing is injected; its presence in the prompt-position lens readout motivated the whole experiment.

numbers.meaning: The number of distinct concepts swept in the summary plot. Each concept contributes one reciprocal-rank-versus-strength curve; the plot shows their median and interquartile band.
One J-lens vector is injected per trial. The experiment tests a single concept at a time, added at every user-turn token.

The paper's stated success rate: the model reports the injected concept in most re-sampled responses. No more precise figure is given in the text; the curve in the plot carries the quantitative detail.

The range of the y-axis. A reciprocal rank of 1 means the injected concept is the model's top output at the report position; values near 0 mean it sits far down the ranking, as at low steering strengths.

The kinds of readout site marked in the widget: the comma after "If so" on the user prompt, the open quotation mark where the report is read, and all remaining assistant-turn positions serving as the position control.
